newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnia's leaders agree on c.bank law-agency.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia's leaders agree on c.bank law-agency.

text.p: Bosnia's Moslem, Croat and Serb leaders agreed on a draft law to form a single central bank after negotiations mediated by U.S. envoys, the state news agency reported on Thursday.

The bank's headquarters will be in Sarajevo and the location of several branch offices will be decided by the French governor of the central bank, Serge Robert, and government leaders, BH press agency said.

Moslem, Croat and Serb members of the collective presidency also agreed in principle on a design for an interim currency until a permanent currency is introduced in Bosnia. The printing of the interim coupons is to begin within the next few months, the agency said.
The agreement followed seven hours of talks on Wednesday led by U.S. envoy Robert Gelbard who pushed to resolve the dispute over the central bank law which has dragged on for six months.
Forming a central bank is a crucial element to clinching a deal with International Monetary Fund (IMF) and for securing $1.4 billion expected to be raised at the donors conference.
Bosnian Serb leaders, who fought against Bosnian statehood, had been reluctant to endorse a single central bank during previous negotiations.

Gelbard, accompanied by officials from the U.S. Treasury Department and the IMF, succeeded in obtaining the agreement in time for the scheduled visit of Secretary of State Madeleine Albright this weekend.
